title: Logarithmic Independence for Local Permutation Iterates
summary: A stronger implication is refuted by a counterexample using constantly many invariants and wires; whether the weakened logarithmic-independence condition guarantees pseudorandomness remains open.

formal_statement.body: For a randomized permutation $P:\{0,1\}^n\to\{0,1\}^n$ in which each output bit depends on only a constant number of input bits, determine whether the $T$-fold composition $P^T$ is a pseudorandom permutation whenever $P^T$ is negligibly far from $\log(n)$-wise independence. This conjectured implication is a weakened form of a refuted stronger conjecture: the known counterexample distinguishes a constant number of invariants using only a constant number of wires, while that approach does not apply when $\omega(1)$ invariants must be maintained. Thus, the unresolved task is to establish or refute the stated pseudorandomness implication under the constant-locality condition. [S1]

scope.domain: Pseudorandomness and limited independence for iterated constant-locality randomized permutations.
assumptions: Each output bit of P depends on only a constant number of input bits.
The T-fold composition of P is negligibly far from log(n)-wise independence.
parameters: P: randomized permutation from n-bit strings to n-bit strings
n: input and output bit length
T: number of times P is composed
scope.unresolved_remainder: Establish or refute whether the T-fold composition being negligibly far from log(n)-wise independence implies that it is a pseudorandom permutation under constant locality.

citations.label: When Simple Permutations Mix Poorly: Limited Independence Does Not Imply Pseudorandomness

progress.summary: The paper explicitly states this as Conjecture 3, a weakened variant not refuted by its counterexample. That counterexample distinguishes a constant number of invariants using a constant number of wires, an approach that does not apply to omega(1) invariants.
citation_labels: Jesko Dujmovic et al., When Simple Permutations Mix Poorly: Limited Independence Does Not Imply Pseudorandomness
